prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System(CBTC): underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering-hours; protection overrides regulation; automation requires trusted communications,verified routes/positions,recorded handback. Operations Control Centre’s Line Traffic Controller owns recovery/incidents/regulation,restricts untrusted control,receives cybersecurity notifications,stops unscripted commissioning trials. Signal Maintenance Engineer(Maple)/controller concur resets; engineer verifies manual-route protection; Cyber Security Officer approves security-sensitive access,correlates events without altering safety paths,classifies availability impacts,investigates audits. East Junction Interlocking(Falcon) produces Axle Counter Reset Request; holds routes/points until safe release; forbids locked/approach resets; rejects invalid-signature/expired-certificate/out-of-window messages. West Junction Interlocking produces Route Release Exception List,rejects protection conflicts. North District Zone Controller(Marble)/South District Zone Controller(Orchid) validate separation/authority/locking; transfers require odometry/validation/reissue; North validates Temporary Speed Restriction Notice; South inhibits automatic routing with manual occupancy. Atlas Onboard Controller(Kestrel): initialization/protected-manual/automatic-train-operation/fallback/cutout; enforces authority/speed/doors/braking,reports faults/checksums/readiness. Dual Channel Odometer disagreement invalidates location; uncertain location/missing authority requires restricted-manual. Both report security diagnostics without cryptographic disclosure. Train Radio Modem reports loss; Wayside Radio Access Network failure reduces throughput. Voice Dispatch Console authorizes restrictions,joins incident procedures for changed instruction methods. Revenue Train Operator repeats instructions,sends Test Train Clearance Memo,no passenger-service cybersecurity administration. Platform Screen Door Controller: protected-local until verified stopping; authenticated approved coordination/testing interfaces only. Metro Operations Control System(Lantern) sends Crew Login Token Bundle,distinguishes command/lock/occupancy,preserves alarms; memo precedes non-revenue security exceptions. Service Timetable Server supplies context; Passenger Information Gateway receives reconciled predictions/platform-updates; both monitored for compromise. Maintenance Diagnostic Server(Quarry) protects evidence,compares Brake Curve Checksum Log,no trust bypass. Cryptographic Key Management Appliance: approved certificates,renewal/revocation,named-account/MFA/separated-duty administration. Audit evidence synchronized,generator-unalterable,governance-retained. Review responsibilities after timetable/radio/control-center changes or integrity incidents. Commissioning requires approved-release baseline checks(onboard/odometer/modem/wayside);

New part:
S233: Metro Operations Control System uses the status snapshot to confirm that platform interface conditions are suitable before authorizing the associated commissioning scenario.
S234: The Platform Screen Door Controller shall be included in end-to-end tests that confirm safe coordination between platform equipment, train stopping position, and supervised door enablement.
S235: The Service Timetable Server shall provide trial schedules that exercise normal headways, recovery margins, terminal reversals, and junction conflicts without carrying passengers.
S236: The Passenger Information Gateway shall be observed during operational rehearsal to confirm that public-facing messages remain consistent with the planned commissioning condition.
S237: Voice Dispatch Console procedures shall be rehearsed for test-train dispatch, abnormal stop instructions, evacuation coordination, and return to depot instructions.
S238: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server shall collect commissioning diagnostics so that intermittent radio, odometry, controller, and interlocking events can be reviewed before acceptance.
S239: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance shall be confirmed as available, synchronized with the approved security baseline, and capable of supporting commissioning operations without manual workarounds.
S240: Readiness reviews shall be held at the completion of each stage and shall include representatives from operations, signalling maintenance, rolling stock, communications, safety assurance, and cyber security.
S241: A Signal Maintenance Engineer shall verify that field defects raised during test running have been closed, deferred with approved controls, or assigned to a post-commissioning monitoring plan.
S242: A Cyber Security Officer shall confirm that access controls, event monitoring, operator accounts, and security incident escalation paths are effective before revenue operation is recommended.
S243: Operational rehearsal shall use realistic degraded scenarios including radio coverage loss, failed train initialization, controller switchover, interlocking unavailability, and control center workstation failure.
S244: The rehearsal shall demonstrate that the Line Traffic Controller can maintain safe service regulation while the Revenue Train Operator follows onboard indications and rulebook instructions.
S245: Acceptance for revenue service shall require completion of planned test cases, closure of safety-critical defects, successful rollback demonstration, and approval of the operations readiness record.
S246: No open defect shall be accepted for revenue service unless its operational restriction, maintenance response, and passenger impact have been assessed and approved by the readiness review authority.
S247: Final entry into revenue service shall occur only after management confirms that training, documentation, staffing, spare equipment, monitoring arrangements, and emergency procedures are in place for sustained operation.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
